q: A Bill is deemed to be a Money Bill, within the meaning of the Constitution, if it contains only provisions dealing with the matters specified in:

options.A: Article 110 of the Constitution
options.B: Article 112 of the Constitution
options.C: Article 114 of the Constitution
options.D: Article 266 of the Constitution

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salaries and allowances payable to the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.
2. The pensions payable to or in respect of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Grants-in-aid to the States under Article 275 of the Constitution are:

options.A: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Voted by the Lok Sabha as part of the Demands for Grants
options.C: Paid out of the Public Account of India
options.D: Paid out of the Contingency Fund of India

q: Besides the items of expenditure specified in Article 112(3) of the Constitution, other expenditure can be treated as 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India where:

options.A: The Finance Minister so directs
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee so recommends
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General so certifies
options.D: It is declared by the Constitution or by Parliament by law to be so charged

q: Under Article 266(2) of the Constitution, all public moneys received by or on behalf of the Government of India, other than the revenues and loans credited to the Consolidated Fund, shall be credited to:

options.A: The Public Account of India
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.C: The Consolidated Fund of the State concerned
options.D: A deposit account with the Reserve Bank of India

q: Under Article 279 of the Constitution, the 'net proceeds' of a tax or duty, for the purpose of distribution between the Union and the States, are ascertained and certified by:

options.A: The Finance Commission
options.B: The Ministry of Finance
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whose certificate is final
options.D: The Reserve Bank of India

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The proceeds of a surcharge on taxes levied by the Union under Article 271 of the Constitution form part of the Consolidated Fund of India and are not shared with the States.
2. A cess levied for specific purposes is likewise excluded from the divisible pool of taxes shared with the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The recommendations of the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution are:

options.A: Binding on the Government of India
options.B: Enforceable by the Supreme Court
options.C: Advisory in character, and not binding on the Government
options.D: Binding only in respect of the States

q: The oath or affirmation made by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India before entering upon his office is in the form set out for the purpose in:

options.A: The Third Schedule to the Constitution
options.B: The First Schedule to the Constitution
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.D: The General Financial Rules

q: A Vote on Account, by which grants are made in advance in respect of the estimated expenditure for a part of the financial year, is generally passed by the Lok Sabha:

options.A: After detailed examination of the estimates by the Estimates Committee
options.B: Only after the Appropriation Bill is passed
options.C: After the Demands are examined by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Without detailed discussion of the estimates, pending their detailed consideration

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Vote on Account from an advance out of the Contingency Fund of India?

options.A: A Vote on Account is an advance made by the executive, while the Contingency Fund advance is voted by Parliament
options.B: A Vote on Account is a grant voted by the Lok Sabha in advance for a part of the year, while an advance from the Contingency Fund is made by the executive to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament
options.C: Both are made by the executive without the vote of Parliament
options.D: There is no difference between the two

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'exceptional grant' from a 'vote of credit'?

options.A: An exceptional grant is made for a special purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year, while a vote of credit is granted for an unexpected demand which, by reason of its magnitude or indefinite character, cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in the Annual Financial Statement
options.B: An exceptional grant is voted after the year is over, while a vote of credit is voted in advance
options.C: An exceptional grant relates to charged expenditure, while a vote of credit relates to voted expenditure
options.D: There is no difference between the two

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Supplementary Grant from an Excess Grant?

options.A: A Supplementary Grant is voted after the close of the year, while an Excess Grant is voted during the year
options.B: A Supplementary Grant relates to charged expenditure only, while an Excess Grant relates to voted grants only
options.C: There is no difference between the two
options.D: A Supplementary Grant is voted during the financial year when the amount authorised for a service is found to be insufficient, while an Excess Grant is voted after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the grant

q: Re-appropriation of funds from one grant (Demand) to another grant is:

options.A: Permissible with the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Permissible with the concurrence of the FA&CAO
options.C: Permissible with the approval of the Railway Board
options.D: Not permissible, as re-appropriation can be made only within the same grant

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'surrender' of funds from 're-appropriation' of funds?

options.A: Surrender is a transfer of funds from one head to another within a grant, while re-appropriation is the return of savings to the Government
options.B: Surrender is the return of anticipated savings in a grant to the Government, while re-appropriation is the transfer of funds from one head of account to another within the same grant
options.C: Both mean the return of savings at the end of the year
options.D: There is no difference between the two

q: The members of the Estimates Committee of Parliament hold office for a term of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: Three years
options.C: Two years
options.D: One year

q: One of the functions of the Estimates Committee of Parliament is to:

options.A: Examine the accounts of public undertakings
options.B: Suggest alternative policies in order to bring about efficiency and economy in administration
options.C: Review the rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.D: Certify the Appropriation Accounts of Railways

q: The members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament are:

options.C: Appointed by the President of India
options.D: Nominated by the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs

q: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways does NOT ordinarily consider:

options.A: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways
options.B: The annual reports of the Ministry of Railways
options.C: National basic long-term policy documents presented to the Houses
options.D: Matters of day-to-day administration of the Ministry of Railways

q: Under the framework of the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI), public-sector auditing comprises three broad types, namely:

options.A: Financial audit, performance audit and compliance audit
options.B: Internal audit, external audit and vigilance audit
options.C: Pre-audit, post-audit and concurrent audit
options.D: Central audit, local audit and resident audit

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes statutory audit from internal audit in respect of reporting?

options.A: Statutory audit reports to the management of the Railway, while internal audit reports to Parliament
options.B: Both report to the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Statutory audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General reports, through the President, to Parliament, while internal audit reports to the management of the Railway itself
options.D: There is no difference in their reporting

q:
Consider the following statements:

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Performance audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is also popularly described as:

options.A: Propriety audit
options.B: Value-for-Money audit
options.C: Certification audit
options.D: Appropriation audit

q: Which of the following correctly states the position of statutory audit in relation to Government policy?

options.A: Audit can set aside a policy of the Government which it considers wasteful
options.B: Audit frames the policy underlying each item of expenditure
options.C: Audit approval is required before a policy is implemented
options.D: Audit does not sit in judgment over Government policy itself, but examines the implementation of policy and the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of the expenditure incurred under it

q: In audit parlance, an auditor is aptly described as:

options.A: A bloodhound, and not a watchdog
options.B: A watchdog, and not a bloodhound
options.C: An investigator of frauds only

options.C: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.D: The Railways Act, 1989

options.C: In the Public Account of India only
options.D: On the assets side, as it represents an amount recoverable by, or awaiting adjustment in favour of, the Railway

q: Deposits lying in the Public Account of India which remain unclaimed for more than three years are:

options.A: Refunded to the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: Transferred to the Contingency Fund of India

options.A: The National Small Savings Fund, forming part of the Public Account of India
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India as tax revenue
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The Post Office Savings Bank only, outside the Government accounts

options.A: Loans granted by international financial institutions for budgetary support

options.C: Advances granted to Government servants for house building
options.D: Market borrowings raised through dated securities

options.A: Traffic accounts and the accounting of earnings

options.A: The Indian Audit and Accounts Service

options.A: 1 only
